dedupe_keys.name: ipcc waste model 2006 guidelines first order decay spreadsheet for solid waste disposal methane

description: The IPCC Waste Model is the spreadsheet that implements the first-order decay method of the 2006 IPCC Guidelines for National Greenhouse Gas Inventories to estimate methane emitted from solid waste disposal sites year by year. It is published by the Task Force on National Greenhouse Gas Inventories, whose technical support unit is hosted by the Institute for Global Environmental Strategies in Japan, alongside Volume 5 (Waste) of the guidelines, which also covers biological treatment, incineration and open burning, and wastewater. Users enter historical waste disposal by composition or by waste stream, the share going to managed and unmanaged sites, and parameters such as degradable organic carbon, decay rate by climate zone and methane correction factors; the model returns methane generation and emissions over time with IPCC default values available for every region. It is designed for national inventories but is widely applied to cities and single landfills. The Excel file and the guideline chapters are free to download. Caveats: default parameters are generic and uncertain, results are sensitive to decay rates and historical disposal data, and the 2019 Refinement updated some factors that this 2006 spreadsheet does not include. Simulation uses: estimating landfill methane for climate adaptation and mitigation scenarios, and setting baselines for waste sector investment appraisal. Related records: the machine-readable IPCC 2006 waste emission factors (data-waste-treatment-disposal-emission-factors-ipcc-2006-vol-5-machine-readable-p02950), and LandGEM (model-landgem) and the CARB Landfill Gas Tool (model-carb-landfill-gas-tool), which use similar decay methods.
